sentences.english_text: The next act was an animal act.
The man came out with six trained dogs, and as Drippy left the stage, still clinging to the Indian Club, he brushed up against one of the dogs and got caught in his fur.
When the audience saw the dogs, they applauded.
And Drippy thought, they're applauding me again.
The trainer of the dog said, jump!
And the dog, Drippy was on, jumped through a hoop.
The audience applauded.
Wait, you haven't seen anything yet.
He had no idea, of course, what was coming next, but he knew that if he was part of it, it must be exciting.
The trainer said, now ladies and gentlemen, you are about to witness one of the most amazing acts in the history of the theater.
This act has been performed before crowned heads all over the world.
I want you to meet Prince.
And onto the stage trotted a beautiful white poodle.
Drippy was beside himself with jealousy.
I'm on the wrong dog.
The white poodle was going to be the star of the show.
Drippy was not sure what the white poodle was going to do, but if it was so great that he had done it before kings and queens, then Drippy wanted to be part of it.
He wanted the audience to be applauding him too.
Quickly, Drippy slid down the leg of the dog that he was on and hurried over to the poodle and climbed up on his neck.
The trainer was saying to the audience, this trick is very dangerous, so I must ask you for absolute silence so that Prince can concentrate on what he's doing.
And the audience was silent.
Everyone was watching the pretty white poodle, but Drippy, who was holding on to the poodle's neck, was thinking, look everyone is watching me.
I wonder if they'll put my picture in the newspaper after this trick.
He wondered what the trick was going to be.
If you're ready Prince, bark once.
Prince barked.
The sound was so loud that Drippy almost fell off his neck.
If you're afraid, bark once.
If you are not afraid, bark twice.
The dog barked twice and again, Drippy almost fell off his neck.
All right Prince, let's go.
